blocks.etymology: From week + end. Originally a Northern England regionalism (see 1903 quotation), in more general use from late 19th century. Compare Saterland Frisian Wiekeneende (“weekend”), West Frisian wykein (“weekend”), Dutch weekeinde (“weekend”), German Low German Wekenenn (“weekend”), German Wochenende (“weekend”).

senses.definition: Happening on or connected with Saturday and Sunday.

examples.en: We decided to take a short weekend trip to the mountains.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi quyết định thực hiện một chuyến đi ngắn ngày cuối tuần lên núi.

examples: I'm wearing my weekend shoes.
wiktionary.gloss: Of, relating to or for the weekend.

examples: a weekend break
wiktionary.gloss: Occurring at the weekend.

idioms.gloss: Used to wish someone a good weekend.
To move a dead body, or otherwise a nonresponsive person (such as due to illness or intoxication), while pretending that the person is alive and conscious.

tatoeba.en: I have to work this weekend.
tatoeba.vi: Tôi phải làm việc vào tuần này.

tatoeba.en: What did you do on the weekend?

tatoeba.en: What did you do over the weekend?
tatoeba.vi: Bạn đã làm gì vào cuối tuần?

tatoeba.en: I go skateboarding at the weekend.
tatoeba.vi: Tôi đi trượt ván vào cuối tuần.

tatoeba.en: He often exercises on the weekend.
tatoeba.vi: Anh ấy hay tập thể dục vào cuối tuần.

wiktionary.gloss: To act with vigour.
